approachQuestion.prompt: Input is a string of n<=200,000 opening and closing parentheses. Return the length of the longest contiguous substring that is balanced and properly nested; empty input returns 0. Example ")()())" -> 4; "(()" -> 2. Choose a method with minimum worst-case processing time; methods tying on time are accepted even if their storage differs.

options.text: Seed an index stack with -1. Push each open index. On close, pop; if empty set the current index as the new base, otherwise update best with current index minus top.
options.feedback: For "(()", the longest valid contiguous substring is the final "()", length 2.

options.text: For every starting index, scan forward with a balance counter. Stop at negative balance; whenever balance is zero update the best length. Return the best across all starts.
options.feedback: Independent start scans are correct and use constant working memory, but can revisit each suffix.

options.text: Return twice the smaller total count of opening and closing parentheses.
options.feedback: For ")(", the two totals are both 1, but the longest valid contiguous substring has length 0 rather than 2.

options.text: Scan left to right counting opens and closes, update best when equal, and reset both when closes exceed opens. Repeat right to left, resetting when opens exceed closes. Return the greatest balanced length found.
options.feedback: The forward scan handles excess closing boundaries; the reverse scan handles excess opening boundaries. Together they find every longest balanced span without storing indices.

feedback.reason: Unmatched boundaries delimit candidate substrings. Either retain their indices or locate balanced spans with two directional balance scans.
details: Seed an index stack with -1. Push each open index. On close, pop; if empty set the current index as the new base, otherwise update best with current index minus top.

The stack top is the boundary before a candidate valid suffix. An unmatched close resets that boundary; an unmatched open stays on the stack. Counting matched pairs alone would combine noncontiguous pieces.

complexityQuestion.prompt: For longest-valid-parentheses-span-optimal, let n be the number of input commands or tokens. Choose the tightest worst-case time and auxiliary-space pair. Input is immutable; output storage is excluded.
constraints: Every stack push/pop and fixed-size operation takes constant time. The implementation is iterative; call-stack space is O(1).
The input may force a stack containing a linear number of entries. No hidden copying of the entire input occurs.

options.text: O(log n) time, O(n) auxiliary space

feedback.reason: Each parenthesis index is pushed and popped at most once.
details: Every index is pushed or popped at most once, giving linear total time. An all-opening string retains n unresolved indices, so the working stack is linear even when the best length is zero.
“O(n) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: A string of n opening parentheses retains n unresolved indices even though its scalar best length is zero.
“O(n²) time, O(n) auxiliary space”: Each parenthesis index is pushed or popped once; valid suffix lengths use index subtraction rather than rescanning substrings.
“O(log n) time, O(n) auxiliary space”: A closing parenthesis at the end may complete the longest suffix, so every character can matter.
